headline: Bajaj Finserv delivered on all verifiable Q1-FY26 guidance commitments in Q2-FY26, with BAGIC holding ROE at ~24% and BALIC posting VNB margin expansion to 17.1% from 10.8% YoY; two full-year targets for BFL AUM/customer additions and BALIC new business premium growth remain open pending H2 data. A one-time GST ITC loss of INR 112 crores compressed BALIC PAT to INR 13 crores versus INR 148 crores in Q2-FY25, introducing a transient but material earnings headwind into H2-FY26.

segments.BAGIC: Combined ratio guidance of 'close to 100%' was met on an adjusted basis at 101.4% ex-1/n regulation (reported 102.3%), flat YoY; ROE guidance of 'reasonably above 20%' was exceeded at ~24% for Q2-FY26 versus 21.4% in Q1-FY26, with management explicitly confirming the figure.
segments.BALIC: VNB margin expanded 630 bps YoY to 17.1% in Q2-FY26 from 10.8% in Q2-FY25, meeting the guided positive delta trajectory for a third consecutive quarter and setting a record half-year VNB; however, PAT collapsed to INR 13 crores from INR 148 crores due to a INR 112 crore GST ITC loss, with management guiding 2 quarters to fully mitigate the ~450 bps annualised margin drag. New business premium growth guidance ('full bloom in H2') remains pending.

keyThemes: BALIC GST ITC headwind: ~450 bps annualised NBM drag expected to persist through H2-FY26; mitigation via product repricing and distributor commission renegotiation is in progress but unquantified

BAGIC acquisition cost creep: underwriting loss widened to INR 92 crores in Q2 from INR 48 crores YoY as higher commissions on preferred lines pressure the combined ratio above 100%, warranting monitoring of expense ratio trajectory

BFL asset quality deterioration: GNPA rose to 1.24% and NNPA to 0.60% in Q2-FY26 versus 1.06%/0.46% YoY, with credit costs remaining elevated in 2-3W and MSME segments; unsecured MSME volumes cut ~25% limiting MSME AUM growth to 12-13% for FY26

Allianz stake acquisition closing: name changes completed, acquisition of 26% stake expected within 'next few months'; capital deployment and any resulting solvency or dividend policy changes are a near-term watchpoint
